pick.headline: El Salvador peace accords signed in Mexico City
pick.summary: On January 16, 1992, the Salvadoran government and the FMLN signed peace agreements at Chapultepec Castle in Mexico City, ending a twelve-year civil war.
pick.significance: The UN-brokered accords ended one of the bloodiest Cold War conflicts in the hemisphere, in which Washington had backed the government.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of January 16, 1992, carried Mexico City XHTV television on guests arriving for the "historic signing" of the Salvadoran peace agreement: Presidents Endara, Gaviria, Perez and Calderon, Felipe Gonzalez, Boutros-Ghali, a delayed James Baker, and Cristiani's delegation.

alternates.headline: The Shah leaves Iran
alternates.summary: On January 16, 1979, Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi left Iran, ostensibly on vacation, amid months of mass protest.
alternates.significance: He never returned. His departure cleared the way for Ayatollah Khomeini's return and the collapse of America's closest ally in the Gulf, with heavy costs for US intelligence and policy in the region.
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of January 16, 1979, listed under Egypt "Shah Expected To Arrive in Aswan January 16" and under Syria ATH-THAWRAH's charge that the Shah and the U.S. were planning counterrevolution in Iran.
